says: A localized-text file (ADML) is refused as invalid when it has no policyDefinitionResources element or when that element has no revision number. The revision is read as a decimal number using invariant (culture-neutral) formatting.

When a localized-text file lists the same text id twice in its string table, or the same presentation id twice in its presentation table, the whole file is refused as invalid. Only the first string table and the first presentation table in the file are read.

When a presentation (the layout of a policy's input controls) has no explicit setting, the controls start as follows. A number box starts at 1, with a spin control and a step of 1. A check box starts unchecked. Combo boxes and drop-down lists are sorted. A drop-down has no preselected item. A setting whose text cannot be read as the expected type falls back to the same start value.

A control in a presentation whose type is not one of the nine known ones (text, number box, text box, check box, combo box, drop-down list, list box, multi-line text box) is dropped and not shown. Known controls are linked to a policy input only when they carry a reference id.

Loading a policy-definition folder reads only the .admx files directly inside it (the extension is matched in any letter case, subfolders are not searched). A file that fails is reported and skipped, and the other files still load. The folder's categories, products, policies and support rules are linked together only after every file has been tried, so references between files resolve whatever the order.
Loading a single policy-definition file loads only that file and reports at most one failure, then links it with everything already loaded.

An ADMX file that cannot be parsed as XML is reported as 'The ADMX XML couldn't be parsed' with the parser's message. Any other fault in it is reported as 'The ADMX is invalid'. Either way the file is skipped.
An ADMX file whose namespace is already owned by an ADMX file that is loaded is refused and reported as 'The <namespace> namespace is already owned by a different ADMX file'.

The localized-text file for an ADMX file is chosen in this order: the folder named exactly like the chosen language code beside the ADMX file; else the first sibling folder whose language part (before the dash) matches the chosen language, e.g. de-AT for de-DE; else the en-US folder. The file has the same name as the ADMX with the extension .adml.
When no localized-text file is found in any of those places, the ADMX file is refused and reported as 'The corresponding ADML is missing'.

A localized-text file that cannot be parsed as XML is reported as 'The ADML XML couldn't be parsed', with the parser's message, and the ADMX file is skipped. Any other fault is reported as 'The ADML is invalid'.

An ADMX file is accepted into the loaded set only when both it and its localized-text file load; then its categories, products, policies and support rules are held for linking and its namespace becomes owned by it. A file that fails leaves nothing behind.

A category whose declared parent cannot be found among the loaded categories is kept as a top-level category instead of being refused. A category with no declared parent is top-level. Only top-level categories appear in the top-level list; every category appears in the full list.

A child product is attached to a parent product that must be defined in the same ADMX file; the parent is looked up under that file's namespace. Only products without a parent appear in the top-level product list; every product appears in the full list.
Each entry of a support rule points at a product if one with that name exists, and otherwise at another support rule. An entry that matches neither points at nothing.

A policy is placed in the category it names, when that category exists. When it does not exist, the policy has no category but is still loaded and listed with all policies. A policy's 'supported on' rule is linked when found, otherwise left empty.
A policy shows a presentation only when it names one and the name resolves to a presentation in its localized-text file. Otherwise the policy has no presentation.
Every category, product, support rule and policy is identified across all loaded files by its namespace, a colon and its own name, so equal names in different files stay distinct.

When a reference to another item is looked up while building, an item from the files being loaded now is preferred over one loaded earlier; otherwise the earlier one is used; if neither exists there is no match.

A displayed name or explanation resolves as follows: empty text stays empty; text not written as $(string.<id>) is shown as it is; $(string.<id>) is replaced by that text from the localized-text file; an id missing from the file leaves the $(string.<id>) text visible.
A policy's presentation reference is honoured only when written as $(presentation.<id>) and the id exists in the localized-text file; any other form or a missing id yields no presentation.

A reference to another item is turned into a full identifier as follows: with a colon and a prefix declared in this ADMX file, the prefix is replaced by its namespace; with a colon and an undeclared prefix, the text is taken literally as the full identifier; without a colon, the item is taken to be in this file's own namespace.

A load failure is shown to the person as: 'Couldn't load <path>: <reason>', with a full stop added when the reason does not already end with one. The reasons are: 'The ADMX XML couldn't be parsed: <detail>', 'The ADMX is invalid: <detail>', 'The corresponding ADML is missing', 'The ADML XML couldn't be parsed: <detail>', 'The ADML is invalid: <detail>', 'The <namespace> namespace is already owned by a different ADMX file'. An unknown kind shows its detail, or 'An unknown error occurred' when there is none.

A policy-definition (ADMX) file is refused as invalid when it declares the same namespace prefix twice. A policy missing its name, display name, registry key or class, or an element missing its id, is also refused. Support rules, products and categories missing their required name or display name are refused likewise.
The ADMX file's own namespace is the one declared as the target; the other declared namespaces are available under their prefixes for references.
A policy applies to the computer when its class is 'Machine', to the user when its class is 'User', and to both when its class is anything else.

A support rule combines its conditions as 'any of' when its first 'or' or 'and' child is 'or', and as 'all of' when it is 'and'. Only the first such child is read. A rule with neither has no conditions and a blank logic. A condition is either a plain product reference or a product range with optional minimum and maximum version numbers.

Products form three levels by position: a top-level product, its major versions (major revisions) and their minor versions (minor revisions). Versions below the first level must carry a version index.
A registry value in a policy is read from its first child: 'delete' means the value is removed, 'decimal' means a number, 'string' means text. A value with none of these has no type.
A policy has on and off settings read from its enabled value, disabled value, enabled list and disabled list; a value or list not present is left empty, so the policy sets nothing for that side.

Policy input elements start with these limits unless the file states otherwise: a number is between 0 and 4294967295, not soft and not stored as text; a text box allows 255 characters, is not required, not expandable and not soft; a list is not additive, not expandable, has no explicit names; a choice list is not required. Settings that cannot be read as the expected type fall back to these.
A policy input element of a type other than number, true/false, text, list, choice or multi-line text is skipped and not offered to the person.

A list element has a name prefix only when it declares a valuePrefix. A list's own registry value name comes from that prefix; for other elements the registry value name comes from the element's valueName, and a name already set is kept.

A policy comment file (CMTX) is refused as a whole when it repeats a namespace prefix, a policy reference or a string id. A comment file that cannot be loaded is treated as 'comments unavailable' for that policy source.

When policy comments are saved, each comment is stored as its own text under a unique id, and its policy is referenced through a short prefix standing for the policy's namespace. Each distinct namespace gets one prefix; the text of every comment gets a new running number so ids never collide. A policy id with no colon cannot be saved.

When the comment file is read back into comments, each policy is identified by its prefix's namespace and its comment id; the comment text is the string the comment points to. A comment pointing to a prefix or string that is not in the file makes the whole file unreadable.
Saving without a path overwrites the file the comments were loaded from.
A saved comment file always states revision 1.0, schema version 1.0 and minimum required revision 1.0, whatever its source declared, and holds every prefix, comment and string currently held.
When the program's settings key in the Windows registry cannot be created or opened, no error is shown: the program carries on without stored settings.
Reading a setting returns the stored value, or the given default when the setting is absent or the settings key could not be opened.
Saving a setting writes it under the settings key; when the key could not be opened, the setting is silently not saved.
A setting counts as present only when the settings key opened and the value exists.
The ADMX details window lists only the policies, categories (including nested ones), products and support rules that are defined in the chosen ADMX file, each by its own id and display name.

The category details window enables its 'parent' button only when the category has a parent. The parent field shows the parent's name; when the category names a parent that was never loaded it shows '<orphaned from <parent id>>'; with no parent it is empty.

statement: When several sibling language folders share the chosen language, such as de-AT and de-CH for de-DE, the one used depends on the order Windows lists folders. The code states no preference among them.

assumed.why: The choice rests on the operating system's folder listing order, which no file in the code fixes.
assumed.ifWrong: People may see definitions in a different regional variant of their language than expected.

evidence.shows: First matching sibling folder with a usable file is taken, in listing order.
